newsitem.title: INDIA: India police claim evidence against Rao in bribe case.
newsitem.headline: India police claim evidence against Rao in bribe case.

text.p: India's federal investigating agency said on Tuesday it had sufficient evidence against former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao and 20 others indicted in a bribes-for-votes case to press for a trial.

"There are sufficient charges against each accused and we should proceed with the trial in the case," A.K. Dutt, lawyer for the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), told a special court hearing the case.
"The CBI has incontrovertible evidence against all the accused," Dutt told Reuters.

He said those indicted, mostly politicians including Rao's former cabinet colleagues, had been linked with payments to four parliamentary deputies to defeat an opposition no-confidence vote in parliament in 1993.
Rao's lawyer, R.K. Anand, said all those indicted had denied involvement in the case.
"The charges have yet to be accepted by the court. I will rebut them, possibly tomorrow or on Thursday," Anand told Reuters.
Rao, who led his Congress party to its worst ever defeat in general elections last year, has been named in two other cases relating to forgery and cheating. He has denied wrongdoing in all the cases.
Tuesday's hearing was linked to allegations by the opposition that Rao tried to influence a parliamentary vote by bribing four deputies of a tribespeople's party in the eastern state of Bihar.
The CBI has been investigating payments totalling three million rupees ($84,000) made into a bank account held by Suraj Mandal, chief of the Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM) party.
"We expect to complete the CBI's arguments in two days but it could take another month for the trial to begin," Dutt said.
Rao and one more accused were exempted from appearing at Tuesday's hearing after their lawyers pleaded they were unwell.
India's Supreme Court last June told the CBI to speed up its investigations.

Rao was forced to resign as Congress president last September. His successor, Sitaram Kesri, has frequently threatened to withdraw the party's support for Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, who heads a shaky 15-member coalition.

Opposition politicians say Deve Gowda was using the cases against Rao to pressure Congress deputies loyal to the former prime minister to retain their support during parliament's current budget session.
The budget for fiscal 1997/98 (April-March), criticised by the Congress, is expected to be put to the vote later this month in a key test of support for the Deve Gowda government. ($1 = 35.80 rupees)
